source_text: In Ecclesiasten (fragmenta e catenis) 79 Πνεῦμα τὴν ψυχὴν ὀνομάζει· προαίρεσις γάρ ἐστι ποία νοῦ κίνησις· καὶ ὁ ∆αυῒδ· εἰς χεῖράς σου παρατίθημι τὸ πνεῦμά μου· Κύριε Ἰησοῦ, δέξαι τὸ πνεῦμά μου·
thought_title: Spirit names the soul as a deliberate movement of mind
orientation: Eustathius is explaining Ecclesiastes' use of the word 'spirit,' arguing that it refers to the soul understood as a deliberate movement of the mind, and he supports this with biblical quotations.
pass_a_gloss: He calls the soul 'spirit'; for it is a certain deliberate choice, a movement of the mind; and David: 'Into your hands I entrust my spirit'; 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.'

choices.why: Keeps the subject implicit as the author of Ecclesiastes, matching the commentary context; preserves the word order emphasis on 'spirit' as the term being explained.

choices.term: προαίρεσις γάρ ἐστι ποία νοῦ κίνησις
choices.english: for it is a certain deliberate choice, a movement of the mind
choices.why: Renders ποία as 'a certain' to preserve the indefinite quality; keeps 'deliberate choice' as the glossary term and 'movement of the mind' as the appositional explanation.
rejected: for it is some kind of deliberate choice, a movement of mind
for it is a deliberate choice of some kind, a movement of the mind

choices.term: εἰς χεῖράς σου παρατίθημι τὸ πνεῦμά μου
choices.english: Into your hands I entrust my spirit
choices.why: Preserves the literal word order of the Greek quotation, including the prepositional phrase first and the verb 'entrust' matching παρατίθημι.
rejected: I entrust my spirit into your hands
Into your hands I place my spirit

choices.term: Κύριε Ἰησοῦ, δέξαι τὸ πνεῦμά μου
choices.why: Keeps the vocative address and imperative force of δέξαι as 'receive,' matching the brief's identification of this as Stephen's prayer.

bible_refs.note: εἰς χεῖράς σου παρατίθημι τὸ πνεῦμά μου
Κύριε Ἰησοῦ, δέξαι τὸ πνεῦμά μου

pass_b_english: He calls the soul “spirit,” for it is a certain deliberate choice, a movement of the mind. David also says, “Into your hands I entrust my spirit” (Psalm 30:6 LXX / Psalm 31:5). And, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit” (Acts 7:59).

last_rejected.why: English attributes both quotes to David, but second quote 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit' is Stephen's words in Acts, not David's. Source marks only first as David's with καὶ ὁ Δαυίδ.
last_rejected.fix: David also says, 'Into your hands I entrust my spirit.' And, 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit'
last_rejected.ruling: English 'David also says' introduces only the Psalm quote; 'And' introduces the Acts quote separately. No misattribution.

last_rejected.source_quote: εἰς χεῖράς σου παρατίθημι τὸ πνεῦμά μου
last_rejected.why: The LXX Psalm numbering is 30:6, but the Hebrew numbering is 31:5. However, the work brief states Psalm numbering follows the LXX, so dual numbering is unnecessary and potentially confusing; more critically, the verse is Psalm 30:6 LXX (which is 31:5 MT), but the brief says LXX numbering should be followed.
last_rejected.ruling: Dual numbering (30:6 LXX / 31:5 MT) is standard scholarly practice; not misleading. Mere preference, not a major error.
